A.text: A thorough grasp of the medical history lowers the risk of aggravating a medical condition.

B.text: Histories need to be current, so an earlier history left unupdated is not adequate.

cites.section: Oral Treatment for Infants, Children, and Adolescents

C.text: Knowing the oral health risks linked to a medical condition can guide anticipatory guidance, treatment planning, and changes to dental management.

cites.section: Management of Dental Patients with Special Health Care Needs › Background

D.text: For patients with special health care needs, the medical providers should be consulted in addition to taking a thorough history.

cites.section: Management of Dental Patients with Special Health Care Needs › Recommendations

explanation.text: Understanding the history well lowers the chance of aggravating a medical condition during care such as local anesthesia.
The other statements conflict with guidance that histories be current, that condition-specific risks inform planning, and that medical providers be consulted.
